qs.q: A patient with chronic alcoholism presents with neurological symptoms due to Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, caused by a deficiency in thiamine pyrophosphate. Which key metabolic multi-enzyme complex is directly impaired?
o: Glycogen phosphorylase complex regulating hepatic glycogenolysis breakdown rates
ATP synthase rotary complex generating cellular energy across membranes
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase initiating urea synthesis inside liver cells
Glucose 6 phosphate dehydrogenase controlling pentose phosphate pathway flux
Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex linking glycolysis pathways to citric acid cycles
qs.e: Thiamine pyrophosphate is an essential coenzyme for the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and transketolase.

qs.q: A chronic alcoholic develops Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome. This condition is primarily due to a deficiency of which vitamin?
qs.e: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, often seen in chronic alcoholics, is caused by thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency. The note explicitly links 'Wernicke-Korsakoff (thiamine deficiency)'.
